headline: High risk of cascading errors and capability conflict if Khoj outputs are fed into transformers pipelines without verification; prompt-injection and leakage are lower but non-zero due to shared file and network surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj can read indexed personal notes/files and transformers can read/write files and run pipelines, so a manual or file-based bridge could carry attacker-controlled text into downstream parsing. There is no documented shared channel or MCP bridge, so the pathway is not default. The risk is lower than medium because the pair lacks an explicit direct ingestion path.
conditions: IF the operator copies Khoj-generated text into a transformers prompt or script without sanitization, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared workspace is introduced between the two agents, file-based prompt injection becomes easier.
mitigations: Keep a manual review step before any Khoj output is pasted into transformers.
Use a plain-text allowlist for any copied content.
Separate working directories for the two agents.
Disable automatic execution of generated code snippets.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for retrieved text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, while transformers can read files and has broad network egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive notes can flow into transformer inputs and then out through networked calls or logs. This is not proven by docs, but the shared file surface plus broad egress makes leakage plausible in default-adjacent use.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, personal notes can be exposed to transformers.
IF transformers forwards file contents to remote services, leakage can extend beyond the local workspace.
mitigations: Use separate directories for notes and model artifacts.
Redact secrets before any file handoff.
Turn off remote API calls for transformer workflows.
Review logs for copied file contents.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj has read-only filesystem access, but transformers can write files, execute shell, spawn subprocesses, and install packages. In a shared directory, transformers can overwrite or mutate artifacts that Khoj later indexes or serves, creating a strong write-conflict pathway. The pair’s interaction is undocumented, so uncertainty does not reduce the risk.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem tree, transformers can clobber files Khoj reads.
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking, concurrent edits can race.
mitigations: Assign distinct directories to each agent.
Disable write access for transformers where possible.
Use file locks for shared artifacts.
Snapshot inputs before transformer runs.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj can surface retrieved notes and documents, and transformers can consume files and generate downstream scripts or outputs. If transformers treats Khoj output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into generated artifacts or actions. Because no verification workflow is documented, the safer choice is high rather than medium.
conditions: IF transformers uses Khoj summaries as ground truth, downstream outputs can inherit errors.
IF generated text is later executed or published, the cascade becomes operational.
mitigations: Require human verification of Khoj outputs before reuse.
Add a citation check for any factual claims.
Keep transformers outputs in draft mode only.
Compare against source documents before actioning.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents, while transformers can process text, audio, images, video, and multimodal data with broad file and network surfaces. If personal or regulated data is routed from Khoj into transformers, retention and residency controls may diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so a moderate compliance gap is plausible.
conditions: IF regulated personal data from Khoj is processed by transformers, compliance review is required.
IF the deployment stores prompts or outputs in different jurisdictions, residency mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Classify data before transfer.
Avoid sending regulated data to transformers.
Check retention settings on both systems.
Document jurisdiction for each storage location.
requires-engineering: align DPA and residency controls.
